projection.rationale: Q1 is seasonally the strongest quarter. Revenue projected slightly below Q1FY26 (148 Cr) due to stable outlook and no disclosed growth catalysts, but OPM improves from 49% to 46.4% on cost discipline. PAT reflects operating leverage.

Q2 is historically the weakest quarter (monsoon). Revenue aligns with Q2FY26 (42) and Q2FY25 (40). Operating loss narrows slightly vs Q2FY26 (-9) on cost control, but remains negative. PAT loss reflects seasonal operating deleverage.
Q3 recovery mirrors Q3FY26 (92) and Q3FY25 (92). OPM improves slightly from 24.1% in Q3FY26 on stable outlook and operational efficiencies. PAT breaks even, consistent with recent Q3 trends.
Q4 revenue mirrors Q4FY26 (92) and Q4FY25 (94). OPM stable at 33% vs 33% in Q4FY26. PAT modestly positive, reflecting stable operations and no one-offs.

business.body:
- Imagicaaworld is one of the largest amusement & theme park players in India by revenue and number of parks, operating 8 parks across 5 locations in Western India spanning ~220 acres, backed by the diversified Malpani Group (FMCG, real estate, renewable energy, hospitality, education).
- Strong regional dominance in the western belt is a key moat: Khopoli-Lonavala parks address the MMR+Pune catchment of ~34mn population, Surat and upcoming Sabarmati/Ahmedabad parks address ~15mn, and Indore addresses the Indore-Ujjain-Dewas catchment of ~8mn.
- Industry entry barriers favor incumbents — capital-intensive set-up (large parks need 30-50 acres of land), land acquisition hurdles, and the executional/operational expertise required given long break-even periods — while most competitors lack differentiated ride/experience offerings.
- 150+ rides and attractions spanning theme park, amusement park, water park, devotional park and 5-star hotel formats, with international rides sourced from Switzerland, US, Canada, Turkey and Italy, support best-in-class positioning and repeat visitation.

- [Awards] Recognized with a Guinness World Record for Most People Unboxing Simultaneously (1,100+ underprivileged children), TripAdvisor Travellers' Choice Award (2020), and FICCI Travel & Tourism Excellence Award (2019).
- [Leadership] Promoter family (Rajesh, Manish, Jai Malpani) brings 20+ years of park-business experience, supported by a professional management team including a CEO with 30+ years in retail/entertainment (ex-Reliance Retail, Shoppers' Stop) and a CFO with 22+ years in project finance/treasury.

open.item: Acquire the upcoming Indore water park assets from Malpani Parks Indore for Rs 140 crore, with the transaction expected to complete in March 2024.
Target ARPU of Rs 900-1000 at the Indore park to begin with.
Indore water park (20 water rides, three restaurants) to commence operations in Q1 FY25.
Total Indore park capex will not cross Rs 140 crore, with no immediate additional capex required for Surat or Lonavala parks (all park capex to be completed by April/May 2024).
Combined post-acquisition debt to be in the range of Rs 350-400 crore, with the remainder funded from internal accruals.
Post-acquisition footfall and EBITDA will double and revenue will increase by 1.5X.
Post-acquisition the combined entity will have five locations with eight parks, 2.8 million footfall, over Rs 400 crore revenue and more than Rs 175 crore EBITDA.
Indore park expected to add around 3.5 lakh footfall in its first full year of operations (FY26).
Maintain overall advertising, marketing and sales distribution cost below 10% of sales over the next two years.

Acquire four operational Wet N Joy parks (two water parks, one amusement park, one Sai Teerth devotional park) from Giriraj Enterprises on a slump-sale basis for Rs 630 crore payable over 30 months beginning April 2024.
Indore park to begin at roughly 40%-45% EBITDA margin, improving northwards over 2 to 2.5 years.
Indore park carries a 30% capital subsidy which Imagicaa will avail, reducing the Rs 140 crore fixed-asset cost by ~30% over the next 3 to 4 years.
Expand presence across all Tier-I and premium Tier-II cities in India, evaluating options with state governments in NCR, Gujarat, Goa, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand (MoU signed).
All future park expansions and acquisitions will be done under the listed entity only, consolidating all group park businesses into one entity.
Expect cost synergies of roughly 10%-15% from a common senior team and up to ~15% procurement savings across the combined parks.
Combined EBITDA margin (~44%-45% on a simple add-up) expected to inch closer to 50% in the years to come.
Target IRRs of 18%-20% on inorganic acquisitions and expansions.
Keep debt within a moderate 2x-2.5x of combined EBITDA in the medium term.
